title: Functions in Tables and Mapping Diagrams Review Test
description: Identify inputs, reason about unique outputs, and explain representations and counterexamples.

questions.questionText: A table lists x -> y as 21 -> 2, 22 -> 4, 23 -> 6. Is the displayed relation a function?
questions.correctAnswer: Yes; every listed x has one y.
questions.explanation: Read the input column first. Each listed input has one assignment, so these rows define a function on the listed inputs.
options: No; the y-values are different.
Yes; every listed x has one y.
No; x does not start at zero.
Yes; every table is a function.

questions.questionText: A mapping shows arrows 21 -> 5 and 21 -> 9. Which input has conflicting outputs?
questions.explanation: Follow the arrows from 21: one goes to 5 and one to 9. One input with two different outputs fails the test.

questions.questionText: Three arrows are 21 -> 8, 22 -> 8, 23 -> 8. Do converging arrows break the function rule?
questions.correctAnswer: No; each input still has just one outgoing assignment.
questions.explanation: Several arrows may end at the same output. The test concerns arrows leaving each input, not arriving at each output.
options: Yes; an output can receive only one arrow.
Yes; the output must increase.
No; each input still has just one outgoing assignment.
No; every arrow diagram is a function.

questions.questionText: Read the table: input 21 gives 3; input 22 gives 6; input 23 gives 9. What is the output for input 22?
questions.explanation: Find the specified input row and read its paired output. Do not use the input number itself as the answer.

questions.questionText: The stated input set is {21, 22, 23}. Arrows are shown only from 21 and 22. What is missing for a function on that entire input set?
questions.explanation: A function must assign an output to every input in its stated domain, as well as avoiding conflicting outputs.
options: One output assignment for 23.
A different output for every input.
A second arrow from every input.
An arrow from every output back to an input.

questions.questionText: A table contains (21, 2), (22, 5), (21, 2). A student rejects it because x repeats. What is the correction?
questions.correctAnswer: The repeated x has the same y both times, so the displayed relation is a function.
questions.explanation: Identical rows repeat the same assignment. Only different outputs for the same input create a conflict.
options: The repeated x must be deleted even when its output agrees.
The repeated x has the same y both times, so the displayed relation is a function.
It is not a function because every y must be different.
It is a function only if the inputs are sorted.

questions.questionText: A function table has (21, 3), (22, 7), (21, k). What value of k avoids a conflict?
questions.explanation: Input 21 already gives 3. Its second row must agree with that output.

questions.questionText: A mapping has 21 -> 4 and 22 -> 6. Which additional arrow would make the relation fail the function test?
questions.explanation: Input 22 would have outputs 6 and 9. The other arrows have new inputs and create no conflict.

questions.questionText: A table is shown in this order: (23, 8), (21, 4), (22, 6). Which mapping represents exactly the same relation?
questions.explanation: The order of rows can change, but each input-output pairing must stay intact. Reversing arrows changes the relation.

questions.questionText: The table follows the stated rule y = 2x + 1. Its rows include (21, 43) and (23, ?). What fills the missing output?
questions.explanation: Use the supplied rule, not a guessed pattern: 2(23) + 1 = 47.
